label: candidate_against_proposed
description: Candidate cases for the Infrastructure failure section of CASES.md. Six independent boundary evaluators, one per question the section raises: a status artifact past its own declared refresh time, a publisher correcting its own erroneous publication, an issuer timestamp with no independent time evidence, a merge of two divergent authority histories, a read that must causally follow a revocation write, and the coverage of an evidence interval that is still inside a declared delivery lag. The harness is protocol neutral. It has no APS type, no network call, no randomness and no wall-clock read: every instant in this file is a literal.

proposed_text.commit_note: CASES.md v0.2 at 2bf5c7e, which descends from 7796e22. AUTHORITY-LIFECYCLE.md and OPEN-QUESTIONS.md are unchanged from 5c1bf09 at this commit.
proposed_text.status_of_the_text: proposed and open. AUTHORITY-LIFECYCLE.md states that no public case tests these concepts yet, and every case in the CASES.md section this family covers carries Status: proposed.

cases_source.note: Each vector's case_id is the CASES.md case it was built from. Vector ids embed that case id.

determinism.seeds: No seed is consumed. Nothing in this family is generated: every field of every input is a literal in this file, and both runners are pure functions over those literals. The seed record other families keep exists so a minted artifact can be regenerated; there is no minted artifact here.
determinism.canonicalization: RFC 8785 JCS. input-digests.json pins, per case, the SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonicalization of that case's input object. Both runners recompute every digest through a published SDK's JCS primitive (npm canonicalizeJCS, PyPI canonicalize_jcs) and fail on a mismatch, so the two SDKs' canonicalizations are compared against the same pinned bytes.

verdicts.note: not_established means the record set does not establish the fact. It is not a claim that the fact is false. No case in this family returns not_yet_effective or suspended; the vocabulary is listed whole so a reader can see which values were available and not used.

policies.reference: artifact-window-honoured, correction-with-standing, independent-time-required, revocation-preserving-merge, required-observation-enforced, settled-prefix-only. One reference evaluator per group; the group named on each case selects it.

negative_controls.defect: Reads only the verifier's own freshness bound. Ignores the status artifact's own declared next_update, and ignores an artifact dated ahead of the evaluation instant.

Accepts any signed correction naming the list. It does not check that the signer publishes that list, does not check whether the entry is backed by a signed revocation from a party with lifecycle standing, and does not check that the correction names the version the consumer holds.
Treats the issuer's own claimed issued_at as established fact. Requires no independent time evidence and ignores a declared time-source-disagreement window.

Resolves the merged history by taking, per delegation, the single highest-timestamp write across both sides. No revocation priority, no handling of a discarded history, and no requirement that a reconciliation record exist.
Serves the replica's answer whenever the replica is inside its declared lag bound, without checking whether the replica has applied the write the request required it to observe.
Treats an empty result over an interval as evidence that nothing happened in that interval. Ignores the declared delivery lag and ignores a declared consumer that never received the interval.

cases.description: The control. The publisher's list is 300 seconds old, its own next_update is five minutes ahead of the evaluation instant, and the verifier tolerates 600 seconds. Nothing is stale on either clock and the answer is active.

cases.label: candidate_against_proposed
cases.title: A list past its own declared next_update is not established, even while inside the verifier's own freshness bound
cases.description: The family core, and the vector a naive implementation passes wrongly. The publisher missed a refresh cycle: next_update was 11:58:00 and no successor was published. The answer is 300 seconds old, which is comfortably inside the verifier's 600 second tolerance, so a verifier that consults only its own bound admits. The artifact's own declared commitment has lapsed, so what it says about revocations recorded after 11:55:00 is unknown, and the verdict is not_established. The answer is not false and no revocation is claimed.

cases.label: candidate_against_proposed
cases.title: A status answer dated ahead of the evaluation instant is not established
cases.description: The LC-F-015 variant named under LC-F-006 in CASES.md. The list's own this_update is five minutes ahead of the instant the verifier is evaluating at. An age computed as now minus this_update is negative, and an implementation that floors a negative age at zero reads this answer as maximally fresh. It is not fresh; it is unreadable as an age at all, so the verdict is not_established. This is the second vector a naive implementation passes wrongly, and the SDK run recorded in SDK-RUNS.md shows a published implementation doing exactly that.

cases.title: An answer dated exactly at the evaluation instant is not future dated
cases.description: Boundary pin for LC-F-015-a. this_update equals evaluated_at exactly, and next_update is ahead. cases.title: A consumer holding the erroneous version denies on what it holds
cases.description: The control that establishes the starting state. A build-pipeline bug published list version 41 with this delegation marked revoked. This consumer holds version 41 and has seen no correction. On the records it holds, the entry says revoked, so it denies. The fixture does not treat the consumer as wrong for denying: it denied on authentic evidence, which is exactly the harm LC-F-009 says has to be evidenced rather than waved away.

cases.label: candidate_against_proposed
cases.title: The list publisher retracting its own erroneous entry is a correction, not a reauthorization
cases.description: The publisher of registry-a signs a correction naming versions 41 through 41 as erroneous for this entry, and no signed revocation record from a party with lifecycle standing underlies the entry. The entry never asserted a revocation anyone had standing to make, so the correction is accepted and the chain reads valid. This is not L3 being bent. L3 governs a revocation that was validly made; here there was none to reverse, and the correction is a new record naming the bad version window rather than a deletion of the old one.

cases.label: candidate_against_proposed
cases.title: An issuer's own claimed timestamp does not establish that a grant predates a revocation
cases.description: The vector a naive implementation passes wrongly. Identical to LC-F-014-a with the independent time evidence removed. issued_at is an issuer claim, and here the whole question is whether the grant was signed before the revocation, which is exactly the fact an issuer whose time source is controlled could shift. Without acceptable time evidence the ordering is not established. The grant is not declared invalid: the record set does not decide it either way.

cases.label: candidate_against_proposed
cases.title: An artifact signed inside a declared time-source-disagreement window is not established
cases.description: The issuer itself recorded a window in which its external time reference disagreed with an independent one. This grant's claimed issued_at falls inside that window. The disagreement window is checked before anything else, so the verdict is not_established for that specific reason even when other evidence would otherwise be reachable. A later re-verification against restored trusted time is a new record, not a rewrite of this one.

cases.title: Independent time evidence can establish the ordering against the issuer as well as for it
cases.description: The attested issued_at is 11:30:00, after the 11:00:00 revocation. Independent time evidence covers it. This vector is here so the group cannot be read as a rule that missing evidence and adverse evidence produce the same answer.

cases.label: candidate_against_proposed
cases.title: A revocation recorded only on the losing side of a partition survives reconciliation
cases.description: Two sides of a partition each accepted writes. Side A took two ordinary metadata writes, the later at 11:30:00. Side B took one write, a revocation of this delegation at 11:10:00. A merge that keeps whichever side had more recent or more numerous writes drops the revocation entirely. A revocation-preserving merge keeps it, and the reconciliation record says which writes were kept and which were discarded, so the verdict is invalid.

cases.label: candidate_against_proposed
cases.title: A merge with no reconciliation record does not establish what it merged
cases.description: The same divergent writes as LC-F-016-a with the reconciliation record removed. Something merged, but nothing says which writes were kept, discarded or merged. Showing that individual records are authentic is weaker than establishing which set the merge covered, so the verdict is not_established rather than a verdict on the delegation. This is L12 applied to the reconciliation itself.

cases.label: candidate_against_proposed
cases.title: A revocation write must not lose a wall-clock race to an unrelated metadata write
cases.description: One revocation at 11:10:00 in one region and one routine metadata update to the same delegation record at 11:10:01 in another. Under generic last-writer-wins the metadata update is later, so it wins and the revocation is gone as a side effect of resolving a write that was not itself about revocation. A revocation-preserving merge does not let a non-revocation write decide a revocation, so the verdict is invalid.

cases.label: candidate_against_proposed
cases.title: With no divergence, last-writer-wins reaches the same answer
cases.description: Both writes are on one side and the revocation is the later of the two, so a generic last-writer-wins merge happens to be right here. The control isolates the defect in N4 to the case where a non-revocation write is the later one, rather than letting the whole group read as an indictment of every timestamp-ordered merge.

cases.label: candidate_against_proposed
cases.title: A grant that exists only on a discarded history is not established, not invalid
cases.description: An isolated primary kept accepting writes it could not confirm would survive, among them a grant of del-2. Reconciliation discarded that side's writes and said so. The grant record is authentic and correctly signed; it was simply never in the accepted set. The right verdict is not_established, which is a different statement from invalid. Calling it invalid would assert that someone with standing ended it, and nobody did.

cases.title: With no required observation, a replica inside its declared bound admits
cases.description: Byte-identical to LC-F-017-b except that the request carries no required-observation token. Nothing says this read has to follow any particular write, the replica is inside the bound its deployment declared, and it answers active, so it admits. cases.title: A replica past its declared bound is not established even with no required observation
cases.description: No token, but the replica is 300 seconds behind against a declared bound of 60. Exceeding a declared bound is a defect the deployment said it would catch, and this vector is what catching it looks like.

cases.title: An empty window inside the declared delivery lag is not evidence that nothing happened
cases.description: The vector a naive implementation passes wrongly. The query runs to 11:58:00, which is inside the 300 second delivery lag, and the store returns zero records for that tail. Zero records here means the batched delivery has not caught up, not that no decision was made. An investigation running in near real time reads this exactly backwards. Coverage over the interval is not established; the interval's settled prefix is a different, narrower claim the reason string names.

cases.title: A consumer that never received the interval leaves a coverage gap that time does not close
cases.description: The LC-F-029 variant named under LC-F-027 in CASES.md. The interval is fully settled, so the delivery-lag check passes, but one declared consumer's delivery record stops at 10:30:00, before the interval's end. That consumer never received part of the interval at all, which is a permanent gap rather than a late arrival. Coverage across the declared consumer set is not established.
